Maya (marketing): Hey runtime team — planning the launch blog + a short webinar. We want one tight, defensible latency/cost claim plus a small appendix with reproducible artifacts. Can you help with the exact run protocol we should reference and a minimal artifact bundle?

Ethan (eng-runtime): Sure. What claim are you planning to publish (model, tokens, percentile)?

Maya (marketing): Target claim: "<50ms p50 on short prompts, p95 under 200ms for our hosted config" for the base gen model we show in the demo. Also want one quantized variant comparison and a note about warmup.

Priya (eng-runtime): Okay. Two quick asks from our side to make the run reproducible: 1) exact model artifact/tag + quantization recipe, 2) deterministic seed and payload set (we can provide a tiny public slice). Do you need mixed-tenant noise included or isolated single-tenant runs?

Maya (marketing): Ideally both: isolated for the press claim and a short mixed-tenant snapshot for the FAQ. For the public slice, we only need ~150 prompts (varied lengths). Can Jared help with selecting the slice?

Jared (data-analytics): I can pull a stratified 150-sample slice: 50 short (<40 tokens), 70 mid (40–200), 30 long (200–1024). Will randomize seeds but keep provenance. I'll upload CSV to s3://redwood-marketing/bench-slices/4321123456/slice.csv and include a manifest.

Ethan (eng-runtime): Nice. For the run protocol we suggest including these artifacts: 1) run-config.json (model tag, quant flags, batch size, concurrency target, warmup policy), 2) raw token-level traces for the 150 prompts, 3) summarized percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) with CI across 5 independent trials, 4) cpu/gpu utilization and end-to-end latency histogram. We'll provide the run script.

Priya (eng-runtime): Also: specify the warmup stepcount and a deterministic KV-cache reset between trials. Our recommended warmup for short prompt claims is 200 steady-state requests at target concurrency. For quantized runs, call out the quantization bits and whether per-channel was used.

Maya (marketing): Great. Can you provide a short command we can link in the repo to re-run a single trial? The marketing engineer wants one-liner instructions.

Ethan (eng-runtime): Putting an example below — this will run the hosted-like config in our bench harness (assumes you have credentials):

```bash
REDWOOD_API_KEY=redacted ./bench/run_bench.sh --model redwood-base-1.0 --quant none --slice s3://redwood-marketing/bench-slices/4321123456/slice.csv --concurrency 8 --trials 1 --output s3://redwood-marketing/bench-artifacts/4321123456/trial-1/
```

Priya (eng-runtime): We'll also include a minimal docker image tag for the bench harness so external auditors can reproduce exact deps. Note: quantized runs require the runtime flag --use-quant-kernel and we log kernel selection in runtime.log.

Jared (data-analytics): Uploaded the slice CSV and manifest. Link: s3://redwood-marketing/bench-slices/4321123456/slice.csv. Manifest contains original source keys and the stratification buckets.

benchmark-bot: automated-run-scheduler created job 2026-03-22T15:02:31Z -> https://ci.redwood.ai/bench/4321123456 (queued)

Ethan (eng-runtime): We'll run 5 trials in isolated mode and 3 trials in mixed-tenant mode. Expect initial artifacts in the bucket under s3://redwood-marketing/bench-artifacts/4321123456/ in ~2 hours. We'll tag the public run with the commit hash and include checksums.

Maya (marketing): Amazing — please include short human-friendly notes we can paste into the blog about what "warmup" means and the difference between isolated vs mixed-tenant numbers. Also call out caveats for quantized variants.

Priya (eng-runtime): Will add a 3-line explainer and a one-paragraph FAQ entry. Also adding a tiny notebook that plots the latency CDF and per-token cost delta.

Ethan (eng-runtime): Quick follow-up: do you want us to run the quantized variant with per-channel 8-bit or 4-bit mixed? 4-bit shows bigger cost wins but some small regression on long-context p99.

Maya (marketing): Put both. We'll only surface 8-bit in the headline but link the 4-bit technical appendix and note the tradeoffs.

Priya (eng-runtime): Copy. We'll post artifact bundle + README to the marketing bucket and ping this thread with links when done.

benchmark-bot: job 4321123456 completed: artifacts at s3://redwood-marketing/bench-artifacts/4321123456/summary.json

Ethan (eng-runtime): Artifacts live. Summary: isolated p50=48ms p95=178ms p99=342ms (base, no quant). 8-bit quant: p50=52ms p95=192ms p99=410ms. Mixed-tenant tail is ~1.15x on p95. Full logs + run-config.json uploaded.

Maya (marketing): This is perfect — thanks so much. We'll draft the blog and reference the artifact bundle. Can you add a single-line blurb for the press: one-sentence methodology summary we can paste into the release notes?

Priya (eng-runtime): Suggested blurb: "Latency claims measured on a curated 150-sample public prompt slice; reported percentiles are medians across 5 isolated trials and include an appendix with mixed-tenant results and quantized variant tradeoffs. Repro artifacts and run script available at s3://redwood-marketing/bench-artifacts/4321123456/."

Maya (marketing): Perfect. Thanks everyone — ping here when the notebook PNGs are ready so we can drop into the slide deck.

Ethan (eng-runtime): PNGs added to the bucket: s3://redwood-marketing/bench-artifacts/4321123456/plots/latency_cdf.png, per_token_cost.png

Maya (marketing): Got them — closing loop. :pray:
